blocks.en: Text: Galatians 1:1-10
blocks.es_reference: Texto: Gálatas 1:1-10 (RVG)

blocks.en: "I marvel that you are turning away so soon from Him who called you in the grace of Christ, to a different gospel, which is not another; but there are some who trouble you and want to pervert the gospel of Christ. But even if we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel to you than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed." — Galatians 1:6-8 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Estoy maravillado de que tan pronto os hayáis traspasado del que os llamó a la gracia de Cristo, a otro evangelio. No que haya otro, sino que hay algunos que os perturban, y quieren pervertir el evangelio de Cristo. Mas si aun nosotros, o un ángel del cielo os predicare otro evangelio diferente del que os hemos predicado, sea anatema." — Gálatas 1:6-8 (RVG)

blocks.en: Welcome to our study of Galatians. Of all Paul's letters, this one is written in the greatest hurry and the deepest alarm. There is no thanksgiving at the start, no warm word of praise as in his other letters — he goes straight from his name to a cry of astonishment: "I marvel that you are turning away so soon." Something precious was being lost in the churches of Galatia, and Paul knew that if it were lost, the gospel itself would be lost with it. That precious thing was grace. From the first verse to the last, Galatians is Paul's great defense of the gospel of grace against a counterfeit that was creeping in to replace it. So this is where our whole course begins, and the question of this first unit is the most important of all: what is the true gospel, and how do we know a false one when we see it?
blocks.es_reference: Bienvenido a nuestro estudio de Gálatas. De todas las cartas de Pablo, esta está escrita con la mayor prisa y la más honda alarma. No hay acción de gracias al comienzo, ninguna palabra cálida de elogio como en sus otras cartas — pasa directamente de su nombre a un grito de asombro: "Estoy maravillado de que tan pronto os hayáis traspasado." Algo precioso se estaba perdiendo en las iglesias de Galacia, y Pablo sabía que si se perdía, el evangelio mismo se perdería con ello. Ese algo precioso era la gracia. Del primer versículo al último, Gálatas es la gran defensa que Pablo hace del evangelio de la gracia contra una falsificación que se infiltraba para reemplazarlo. Así que aquí comienza todo nuestro curso, y la pregunta de esta primera unidad es la más importante de todas: ¿cuál es el verdadero evangelio, y cómo reconocemos uno falso cuando lo vemos?

blocks.en: An Apostle — Not From Men
blocks.es_reference: Un Apóstol — No de Hombres

blocks.en: Paul opens by staking his authority: "Paul, an apostle (not from men nor through man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father who raised Him from the dead)" (Galatians 1:1). This is not pride. The troublemakers in Galatia were whispering that Paul was a second-rate apostle who had watered down the message to make it easy. So Paul answers at once: his gospel did not come from men and cannot be edited by men. He received it from the risen Christ Himself. This matters for everything that follows. If the gospel were a human invention, men could add to it or change it as they pleased. But it is God's own message, and no man — not Paul, not an apostle, not an angel — has the right to alter it.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo abre afirmando su autoridad: "Pablo, apóstol (no de hombres ni por hombre, sino por Jesucristo y por Dios el Padre que lo resucitó de los muertos)" (Gálatas 1:1). Esto no es orgullo. Los perturbadores en Galacia susurraban que Pablo era un apóstol de segunda categoría que había rebajado el mensaje para hacerlo fácil. Así que Pablo responde de inmediato: su evangelio no vino de hombres y no puede ser editado por hombres. Lo recibió del Cristo resucitado mismo. Esto importa para todo lo que sigue. Si el evangelio fuera una invención humana, los hombres podrían añadirle o cambiarlo a su gusto. Pero es el mensaje propio de Dios, y ningún hombre — ni Pablo, ni un apóstol, ni un ángel — tiene el derecho de alterarlo.

blocks.en: The Gospel Defined: Grace
blocks.es_reference: El Evangelio Definido: La Gracia

blocks.en: Before Paul confronts the false gospel, he names the true one. He greets the churches with "grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ, who gave Himself for our sins, that He might deliver us from this present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father" (Galatians 1:3-4). There is the gospel in a single sentence. It is grace — God's free and unearned favor — and it rests entirely on what Christ has done: He gave Himself for our sins. The good news is not advice about what we must do to climb up to God; it is the announcement of what God has done to come down and rescue us. Christ "gave Himself." The work is finished, the price is paid, and it is received not by earning but by faith. Hold this firmly, because every false gospel we will study in this course attacks it at exactly this point.
blocks.es_reference: Antes de confrontar el falso evangelio, Pablo nombra el verdadero. Saluda a las iglesias con "gracia y paz a vosotros, de Dios el Padre y de nuestro Señor Jesucristo, el cual se dio a sí mismo por nuestros pecados para librarnos de este presente mundo malo, conforme a la voluntad de Dios y Padre nuestro" (Gálatas 1:3-4). Ahí está el evangelio en una sola oración. Es gracia — el favor libre e inmerecido de Dios — y descansa enteramente en lo que Cristo ha hecho: se dio a sí mismo por nuestros pecados. La buena nueva no es un consejo sobre lo que debemos hacer para subir hasta Dios; es el anuncio de lo que Dios ha hecho al descender a rescatarnos. Cristo "se dio a sí mismo." La obra está terminada, el precio está pagado, y se recibe no por mérito sino por la fe. Aférrese a esto, porque todo falso evangelio que estudiaremos en este curso lo ataca exactamente en este punto.

blocks.en: No Thanksgiving — A Letter in Alarm
blocks.es_reference: Sin Acción de Gracias — Una Carta en Alarma

blocks.en: Now comes the shock. Where every other letter of Paul pauses to thank God for his readers, this one does not. Instead: "I marvel that you are turning away so soon from Him who called you in the grace of Christ, to a different gospel" (Galatians 1:6). Notice what they are turning from: not merely from a doctrine, but from Him — from God Himself, who had called them in the grace of Christ. To abandon grace is to abandon God. And notice the words "so soon." The poison works fast. It had been only a short time since they believed, and already the counterfeit was pulling them away.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora viene la sorpresa. Donde toda otra carta de Pablo se detiene a dar gracias a Dios por sus lectores, esta no lo hace. En cambio: "Estoy maravillado de que tan pronto os hayáis traspasado del que os llamó a la gracia de Cristo, a otro evangelio" (Gálatas 1:6). Note de qué se están apartando: no meramente de una doctrina, sino de Él — de Dios mismo, que los había llamado a la gracia de Cristo. Abandonar la gracia es abandonar a Dios. Y note las palabras "tan pronto." El veneno obra rápido. Había pasado poco tiempo desde que creyeron, y ya la falsificación los apartaba.

blocks.en: A Different Gospel — Which Is No Gospel
blocks.es_reference: Otro Evangelio — Que No Es Evangelio

blocks.en: Paul calls the new teaching "a different gospel, which is not another" (Galatians 1:7). There are not two gospels, a Paul-version and an improved version. There is one gospel, and anything else is not a gospel at all but a perversion of it: "there are some who trouble you and want to pervert the gospel of Christ." Who were these troublers? They were teachers, later called Judaizers, who did not deny Christ. They were happy to add Him to their message. But they insisted that faith in Christ was not enough — that to be truly saved a man must also keep the law of Moses, beginning with circumcision. In other words, they preached grace plus works. And Paul says that grace plus anything is no longer grace, and a gospel of grace-plus-works is no gospel at all.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo llama a la nueva enseñanza "otro evangelio. No que haya otro" (Gálatas 1:7). No hay dos evangelios, una versión de Pablo y una versión mejorada. Hay un solo evangelio, y cualquier otra cosa no es evangelio en absoluto sino una perversión de él: "hay algunos que os perturban, y quieren pervertir el evangelio de Cristo." ¿Quiénes eran estos perturbadores? Eran maestros, más tarde llamados judaizantes, que no negaban a Cristo. Con gusto lo añadían a su mensaje. Pero insistían en que la fe en Cristo no era suficiente — que para ser verdaderamente salvo un hombre debía además guardar la ley de Moisés, comenzando con la circuncisión. En otras palabras, predicaban gracia más obras. Y Pablo dice que la gracia más cualquier cosa ya no es gracia, y que un evangelio de gracia-más-obras no es evangelio alguno.

blocks.en: Every false gospel is grace with something added, grace with something taken away, or grace traded for something else. Galatians 1 gives the church both the gospel and the test by which every counterfeit is exposed.
blocks.es_reference: Todo falso evangelio es gracia con algo añadido, gracia con algo quitado, o gracia cambiada por otra cosa. Gálatas 1 da a la iglesia tanto el evangelio como la prueba con que se expone toda falsificación.

blocks.en: Let Him Be Accursed
blocks.es_reference: Sea Anatema

blocks.en: Then Paul says the most severe thing in any of his letters, and he says it twice: "But even if we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel to you than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed. As we have said before, so now I say again, if anyone preaches any other gospel to you than what you have received, let him be accursed" (Galatians 1:8-9). The word translated accursed is anathema — devoted to destruction, cut off from God. Think how strong this is. Paul does not say, "if a false teacher comes." He says, "even if we — even if I, Paul, myself — or an angel from heaven should preach another gospel, let him be accursed." No messenger is so high, no credentials so impressive, that they can overrule the gospel of grace. The message is fixed; the messenger is not above it. This twofold curse is the measuring rod for our entire course: whenever we weigh a teaching, ancient or modern, this is the standard we hold up — does it preach the gospel of the grace of Christ, or does it preach another?
blocks.es_reference: Entonces Pablo dice lo más severo de cualquiera de sus cartas, y lo dice dos veces: "Mas si aun nosotros, o un ángel del cielo os predicare otro evangelio diferente del que os hemos predicado, sea anatema. Como antes hemos dicho, también ahora lo repito: Si alguno os predica otro evangelio diferente del que habéis recibido, sea anatema" (Gálatas 1:8-9). La palabra traducida anatema significa entregado a destrucción, cortado de Dios. Piense cuán fuerte es esto. Pablo no dice, "si viene un falso maestro." Dice, "si aun nosotros — si aun yo, Pablo, mismo — o un ángel del cielo predicare otro evangelio, sea anatema." Ningún mensajero es tan elevado, ninguna credencial tan impresionante, que pueda pasar por encima del evangelio de la gracia. El mensaje es fijo; el mensajero no está por encima de él. Esta doble maldición es la vara de medir de todo nuestro curso: cada vez que pesemos una enseñanza, antigua o moderna, esta es la norma que levantamos — ¿predica el evangelio de la gracia de Cristo, o predica otro?

blocks.en: Not Seeking to Please Men
blocks.es_reference: No Buscando Agradar a los Hombres

blocks.en: Paul ends this opening with a question that exposes the heart of the matter: "For do I now persuade men, or God? Or do I seek to please men? For if I still pleased men, I would not be a bondservant of Christ" (Galatians 1:10). The false teachers softened the gospel to make it pleasant and to win a following. Paul will not. A gospel trimmed to please people is a gospel that has stopped being the gospel. The servant of Christ must speak what God has said, whether men love it or hate it.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo termina esta apertura con una pregunta que expone el corazón del asunto: "Porque, ¿persuado yo ahora a los hombres o a Dios? ¿o busco agradar a los hombres? Pues si todavía agradara a los hombres, no sería siervo de Cristo" (Gálatas 1:10). Los falsos maestros suavizaban el evangelio para hacerlo agradable y ganar seguidores. Pablo no lo hará. Un evangelio recortado para agradar a la gente es un evangelio que ha dejado de ser el evangelio. El siervo de Cristo debe decir lo que Dios ha dicho, ámenlo o ódienlo los hombres.

blocks.en: Inside the Circle: One Gospel, Many Differences
blocks.es_reference: Dentro del Círculo: Un Solo Evangelio, Muchas Diferencias

blocks.en: It is vital to see exactly where this curse falls — and where it does not. Paul pronounces anathema on those who pervert the gospel itself, who change the way a sinner is made right with God. He does not pronounce it on every disagreement between believers. Picture a circle. At its center stands the gospel — that Jesus lived a perfect life, died on the cross for our sins, rose again the third day, and that we must repent, believe in Him, and make Him Lord — together with the essential doctrines that guard it: the Trinity, one God in three Persons, and the authority and infallibility of Scripture. Whoever holds what is inside that circle holds the one true gospel, and is a brother or sister in Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Es vital ver exactamente dónde cae esta maldición — y dónde no cae. Pablo pronuncia anatema sobre los que pervierten el evangelio mismo, que cambian la manera en que un pecador es hecho justo delante de Dios. No lo pronuncia sobre todo desacuerdo entre creyentes. Imagine un círculo. En su centro está el evangelio — que Jesús vivió una vida perfecta, murió en la cruz por nuestros pecados, resucitó al tercer día, y que debemos arrepentirnos, creer en Él y hacerlo Señor — junto con las doctrinas esenciales que lo guardan: la Trinidad, un solo Dios en tres Personas, y la autoridad e infalibilidad de la Escritura. Quien sostiene lo que está dentro de ese círculo sostiene el único evangelio verdadero, y es un hermano o una hermana en Cristo.

blocks.en: "As we have said before, so now I say again, if anyone preaches any other gospel to you than what you have received, let him be accursed." — Galatians 1:9 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Como antes hemos dicho, también ahora lo repito: Si alguno os predica otro evangelio diferente del que habéis recibido, sea anatema." — Gálatas 1:9 (RVG)

blocks.en: Around the outside of the circle lie many matters on which true Christians, who rest on the same grace, have long differed: the mode and meaning of baptism, how we keep the Lord's Supper, foot washing, styles of worship, spiritual gifts, how a church is governed, the roles of men and women in leadership, and the details of the end times. These are not small or unimportant questions, and we should study them with care. But they are not the gospel, and to differ over them is not to preach "another gospel." A Baptist and a Presbyterian may disagree about baptism and still embrace as brothers, because both rest on the grace of Christ. We must not hand out the curse of Galatians 1 to everyone who differs from us; Paul reserves it for those who change the center.
blocks.es_reference: Alrededor del círculo yacen muchos asuntos en que los verdaderos cristianos, que descansan en la misma gracia, han diferido por mucho tiempo: el modo y el significado del bautismo, cómo guardamos la Cena del Señor, el lavamiento de pies, los estilos de adoración, los dones espirituales, cómo se gobierna una iglesia, los roles de hombres y mujeres en el liderazgo, y los detalles de los últimos tiempos. No son preguntas pequeñas ni sin importancia, y debemos estudiarlas con cuidado. Pero no son el evangelio, y diferir sobre ellas no es predicar "otro evangelio." Un bautista y un presbiteriano pueden discrepar acerca del bautismo y aun así abrazarse como hermanos, porque ambos descansan en la gracia de Cristo. No debemos repartir la maldición de Gálatas 1 a todo el que difiera de nosotros; Pablo la reserva para los que cambian el centro.

blocks.en: A careful example. Consider the Seventh-day Adventists. They hold real distinctives that set them apart from many evangelicals — worship on the seventh-day Sabbath, the writings of Ellen G. White (regarded by them as a subordinate "lesser light" that points back to Scripture, not as an addition to the canon), the doctrine of the investigative judgment, and conditional immortality. Yet on the things inside the circle they stand with the gospel: the sinless life, atoning death, and bodily resurrection of Christ, salvation by grace through faith, the Trinity, and the authority of Scripture. For this reason, when evangelical apologists Walter Martin and Donald Barnhouse conducted extensive doctrinal dialogues with Adventist leaders in 1955–56, they concluded, in the resulting book Questions on Doctrine (1957), that Adventists held the essentials of the gospel and belonged inside the circle rather than preaching another gospel — a conclusion that itself provoked real controversy among evangelicals who remained cautious about certain Adventist distinctives, a caution some hold to this day. This is the charity the test requires: we name a teaching "another gospel" only when it changes the gospel itself.
blocks.es_reference: Un ejemplo con cuidado. Considere a los Adventistas del Séptimo Día. Sostienen verdaderos distintivos que los apartan de muchos evangélicos — la adoración en el sábado del séptimo día, los escritos de Ellen G. White (considerados por ellos como una "luz menor" subordinada que apunta de nuevo a la Escritura, no como una adición al canon), la doctrina del juicio investigador, y la inmortalidad condicional. Sin embargo, en las cosas dentro del círculo están con el evangelio: la vida sin pecado, la muerte expiatoria y la resurrección corporal de Cristo, la salvación por gracia mediante la fe, la Trinidad, y la autoridad de la Escritura. Por esta razón, cuando los apologistas evangélicos Walter Martin y Donald Barnhouse sostuvieron extensos diálogos doctrinales con líderes adventistas en 1955–56, concluyeron, en el libro resultante Questions on Doctrine (1957), que los adventistas sostenían lo esencial del evangelio y pertenecían dentro del círculo en lugar de predicar otro evangelio — una conclusión que provocó una controversia real entre evangélicos que permanecieron cautelosos respecto a ciertos distintivos adventistas, cautela que algunos sostienen hasta hoy. Esta es la caridad que la prueba exige: llamamos a una enseñanza "otro evangelio" solo cuando cambia el evangelio mismo.

blocks.en: By contrast — and this looks ahead to the units to come — some movements do not merely differ on the outside matters; they reach into the center and change it. When a group denies the full deity of Christ, or remakes the one God into something other than Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, or sets a new revelation beside the finished work of the cross, it has crossed the line Paul draws here. That is why later in this course we will weigh Mormonism, the Jehovah's Witnesses, and the prosperity gospel by this same standard. The test never changes: not, "do they differ from us?" but, "do they preach the gospel of the grace of Christ, or another?"
blocks.es_reference: Por contraste — y esto mira hacia las unidades por venir — algunos movimientos no solo difieren en los asuntos de afuera; alcanzan el centro y lo cambian. Cuando un grupo niega la plena deidad de Cristo, o rehace al único Dios en algo distinto del Padre, el Hijo y el Espíritu Santo, o pone una nueva revelación al lado de la obra terminada de la cruz, ha cruzado la línea que Pablo traza aquí. Por eso más adelante en este curso pesaremos el mormonismo, los Testigos de Jehová, y el evangelio de la prosperidad por esta misma norma. La prueba nunca cambia: no, "¿difieren de nosotros?" sino, "¿predican el evangelio de la gracia de Cristo, u otro?"

blocks.en: So we begin where Paul begins. The gospel is grace — Christ who gave Himself for our sins, received by faith alone. Any message that adds to that grace, takes away from it, or trades it for something else is a different gospel, and a different gospel is no gospel. This is the truth the rest of Galatians will defend, and it is the test we will carry into every unit of this course.
blocks.es_reference: Así que comenzamos donde Pablo comienza. El evangelio es gracia — Cristo que se dio a sí mismo por nuestros pecados, recibido solo por la fe. Cualquier mensaje que añada a esa gracia, que le quite, o que la cambie por otra cosa, es otro evangelio, y otro evangelio no es evangelio. Esta es la verdad que el resto de Gálatas defenderá, y es la prueba que llevaremos a cada unidad de este curso.

The definition of the true gospel and the test for every counterfeit

sa.prompt: Who is the author of this letter, and why does he stress that his apostleship is 'not from men'?
sa.model: The author is Paul. He opens by insisting his apostleship is not from men nor through man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father. The troublers in Galatia claimed Paul was a lesser apostle who had softened the message. Paul answers that his gospel did not come from men and cannot be edited by men; he received it from the risen Christ Himself. If the gospel were a human invention, men could change it at will. Because it is God's own message, no one — not Paul, not an apostle, not even an angel — has the right to alter it.

sa.prompt: What is the true gospel as Paul defines it in this opening?
sa.model: Before confronting the false gospel, Paul names the true one: Christ gave Himself for our sins to deliver us from this present evil age. That is the gospel in one sentence. It is grace — God's free and unearned favor — and it rests entirely on what Christ has done, not on what we do. The good news is not advice about climbing up to God; it is the announcement that God came down to rescue us. Christ's work is finished, the price is paid, and it is received by faith, not by earning. Every false gospel attacks grace at exactly this point.

sa.prompt: Why does Paul give no thanksgiving here, and what does 'I marvel that you are turning away so soon' reveal?
sa.model: Every other letter of Paul begins with thanks for his readers, but Galatians does not. The omission is deliberate: Paul is alarmed. He says they are turning away not merely from a doctrine but from Him — from God Himself, who called them in the grace of Christ. To abandon grace is to abandon God. The words 'so soon' show how fast the poison works; only a short time after believing, the counterfeit was already pulling them away. The missing thanksgiving itself signals that the gospel is at stake.

sa.prompt: Explain Paul's phrase 'a different gospel, which is not another.'
sa.model: Paul means there are not two valid gospels, an original and an improved version. There is only one gospel, and anything else is not a gospel at all but a perversion of it. The troublers wanted to pervert the gospel of Christ. This is why the matter is so serious: to change the gospel is not to offer a fresh option but to destroy the only good news there is. A 'different gospel' is, in truth, no gospel.

sa.prompt: Who were the Judaizers, and what was their error?
sa.model: The troublers, later called Judaizers, did not deny Christ; they were willing to add Him to their message. But they insisted that faith in Christ was not enough — that to be truly saved a person must also keep the law of Moses, beginning with circumcision. In other words, they preached grace plus works. Paul's verdict is that grace plus anything is no longer grace, and a gospel of grace-plus-works is no gospel at all. This was the first false gospel, and it is the pattern every later counterfeit follows: adding human requirements to the finished work of Christ.

sa.prompt: What does Paul mean by 'let him be accursed,' and why is this so severe?
sa.model: Paul says the most severe thing in any of his letters, and twice: even if we, or an angel from heaven, preach another gospel, let him be accursed. The word accursed is anathema — devoted to destruction, cut off from God. The severity is the point. Paul does not merely warn against false teachers; he says that even he himself, or an angel, would fall under the curse if he preached another gospel. No messenger is high enough to overrule the gospel of grace. The message is fixed; the messenger is not above it. This is the measuring rod for the whole course.

sa.prompt: What is the significance of Paul saying 'even we, or an angel from heaven'?
sa.model: By naming the highest possible authorities — an apostle (himself) and an angel from heaven — and placing them under the curse, Paul makes the point as strong as it can be made. No messenger, however impressive his credentials, stands above the gospel. A teaching is not true because a respected leader or a heavenly being delivers it; it is true only if it is the gospel of the grace of Christ. We test the message, not by the rank of the messenger, but by the standard Paul has fixed.

sa.prompt: What does Galatians 1:10 teach about not seeking to please men?
sa.model: Paul ends the opening by asking whether he seeks to please men, and answers that if he still pleased men he would not be a servant of Christ. The false teachers softened the gospel to make it pleasant and win a following. Paul will not. A gospel trimmed to please people has stopped being the gospel. The servant of Christ must say what God has said, whether men love it or hate it. This guards us today: we do not measure a gospel by how comfortable or popular it is, but by whether it is faithful to the grace of Christ.

sa.prompt: Using the picture of the circle, explain the test for what is and is not 'another gospel.'
sa.model: The lesson pictures a circle. At its center stand the gospel — Christ's perfect life, His death for our sins, His resurrection, received by repentance and faith — and the essential doctrines that guard it, the Trinity and the authority of Scripture. Whoever holds these holds the gospel and is a brother or sister in Christ. Around the outside lie matters on which true Christians differ: baptism, the Lord's Supper, worship style, church government, the roles of men and women, the details of the end times. Such differences are not 'another gospel.' The curse of Galatians 1 falls only on those who change the center — who add to, subtract from, or trade away the grace of Christ. That is the test we carry through the course.

sa.prompt: Summarize the central truth of Unit 1: what does Galatians 1:1-10 teach before the rest of the letter unfolds?
sa.model: Before Galatians defends anything else, it defines the gospel and gives the test for every counterfeit. The gospel is grace — Christ who gave Himself for our sins, received by faith alone. Paul marvels that the Galatians are turning so soon from the God who called them in that grace to a different gospel, which is no gospel. The troublers preached grace plus the law, and Paul pronounces a twofold curse on anyone — even an apostle or an angel — who preaches another gospel. The central truth of Unit 1 is that there is one gospel of grace; any message that adds to it, takes from it, or trades it away is a different gospel, and this is the measuring rod for all that follows.
